title: The Duration of Life

full_text:
When the Creator created the world and appointed the years of life to each living creature, the Donkey came first and was offered thirty years. The Donkey sighed, "Lord, thirty years of carrying heavy sacks to the mill, being beaten with sticks, and eating thistles is far too weary a burden. Spare me half of them!" And eighteen years were taken away.

Next came the Dog, who was offered thirty years. "Lord," wept the Dog, "running, barking at thieves, losing teeth, and lying stiffly in corners is too long a misery. Give me fewer!" And twelve years were removed.

Next came the Monkey, who begged for relief from thirty years of making silly faces to amuse ungrateful spectators, and ten years were lifted from him.

Finally came Man, proud and joyful, who was offered thirty years. "Thirty years?" protested Man. "Just when I build my house and plant my fields, I must depart? Give me more!"

The Creator granted him the eighteen years refused by the donkey, the twelve years refused by the dog, and the ten years refused by the monkey.

Thus it is that Man lives his first thirty years in human vigor and joy. Then follow the donkey years, bearing heavy burdens of household toil; then the dog years, sitting watchful in the corner, grumbling and guarding; and finally the monkey years, silly and weak, mocked by the young as age takes its toll.
moral: Every stage of life has its appointed character; peace comes from accepting each season with grace.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Duration of Life"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
